manuscript_claim: On unconstrained student exam handwriting, OCR engines exhibit high baseline error rates (CER > 0.90) dominated by line segmentation and header formatting challenges.
statistical_significance: Empirical evaluation on locked test partition

manuscript_claim: The corrected OpenCV 4.5+ MinAreaRect deskew algorithm resolves coordinate convention flips, achieving angular estimation error <= 0.02 deg across +/-10 deg fixtures.
Dual-range HSV red-ink isolation completely eliminates examiner tick and margin grade contamination (0.0% leakage vs 38.5% in raw OCR).

Under an identical frozen rubric grader, uncalibrated OCR causes a catastrophic evaluation collapse (mean Delta = -12.92 to -14.0 marks; QWK collapses to 0.00 - 0.04), dropping student grades by over 93%.

The frozen rubric grader on human oracle transcripts achieves near-perfect agreement with teacher gold (MAE 0.833 marks, QWK 0.9268), proving the scoring engine is highly accurate when transcription errors are removed.

When structural recognition errors drop entire question segments, standard CER/WER and token edit metrics show negative correlation with localized damage (r = -0.16 to -0.17), proving structural routing failures dominate character edit metrics.
Uncertainty-aware selective human routing achieves 0.988 hybrid QWK and reduces human grading workload by 79.2% by selectively escalating the top 20% highest-uncertainty scripts.
statistical_significance: Conformal 90% empirical coverage validated on locked test

manuscript_claim: The recognition and grading pipeline retains 97.9% performance retention under zero-shot transfer to Stanford CS224N-style conceptual exam rubrics.
